title: Data Retention and Deletion SLA Template
content:
Purpose
This annex describes the agreed data retention, secure deletion, and related service-level objectives between [Customer] ("Customer") and Redwood Inference, Inc. ("Provider") as an attachment to the Data Processing Agreement and Master Services Agreement. It is intended to align expectations for how long classes of data are retained, how deletion requests are handled, timelines for permanent removal (including backups), and evidence/audit mechanisms.

Scope and Applicability
Applies to all personal data and Customer data processed by Provider pursuant to the Agreement unless otherwise stated in the Agreement or required by applicable law. For clarity: (a) system-generated telemetry and operational logs are in scope; (b) model weights and derivative artifacts that do not contain Customer personal data are out of scope for erasure requests but may be subject to retention controls in the Agreement; (c) Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments may have different operational timelines — see Section 4.

Definitions
- "Deletion Request": a Customer-initiated request to delete specified Customer Data or to exercise erasure rights under applicable data protection laws.
- "Permanent Deletion": destruction or irrecoverable erasure of data from active storage and backups such that it cannot be reconstructed using Provider's available tools.
- "Backup Window": the maximum period during which copies of data may exist in backups or disaster recovery stores.

Retention Categories and Default Periods
The parties may map their data classes to the categories below. Default retention periods (subject to Customer-specific configuration and lawful hold exceptions):
- Transactional and customer-configured content (e.g., indexable documents uploaded for inference): 90 days after last access or as configured by Customer.
- Prompt/Request logs (text of calls to the API): 30 days by default; configurable to 0, 7, 30, 90, or 365 days per plan.
- Aggregated usage metrics and billing records: 7 years for financial and audit compliance.
- Operational logs and traces (non-identifying): 180 days.
- Security logs and forensic artifacts: 24 months or as required for incident investigation.
- Backups and cold storage snapshots: Backup Window default 90 days unless otherwise negotiated.

Controller/Processor Notes
Where the Agreement designates the Customer as Controller and Provider as Processor, Provider will only retain personal data for as long as necessary to provide the services and in accordance with Customer instructions (subject to legal holds and obligations). Customer may specify shorter retention periods via the Console or by written notice to Provider as described in the Agreement.

Deletion Requests — Operational SLA
Provider will acknowledge and begin processing valid Deletion Requests as follows (SLA measured from the time Provider acknowledges receipt):
- Hosted API: initial acknowledgement within 24 hours; complete removal from active systems within 48 hours; permanent deletion (including primary replicas) within 30 calendar days; permanent deletion from Disaster Recovery backups within Backup Window (default 90 days).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): initial acknowledgement within 48 hours; complete removal from active systems within 5 business days; permanent deletion from backups within Backup Window or negotiated timeline.
- Private (customer-managed infrastructure): Provider will provide deletion scripts, documentation, and verification procedures. Provider will assist in deletion upon Customer request; Customer is primarily responsible for executing final deletion on Customer-managed storage unless otherwise agreed. Provider assistance SLA: initial acknowledgement 3 business days; assistance completion timeline to be mutually agreed case-by-case.

Proof of Deletion and Attestation
- Provider will, upon Customer's written request, provide a deletion attestation describing the actions taken, locations cleaned, and relevant timestamps. Attestations will be provided within 10 business days of completion of deletion activities.
- For Hosted and Dedicated services, attestations include system logs and deletion job IDs. For Private deployments, attestations will include scripts run and command output from Customer-governed systems where Provider had access.

Exceptions and Legal Holds
- Provider may retain copies or limit deletion where required by applicable law, regulatory obligations, or where data is subject to a lawful hold requested by Customer. Provider will notify Customer of any such legal hold unless prohibited by law.
- If permanent deletion would interfere with ongoing security investigations or incident remediation, Provider may retain limited data for the duration of the investigation and will notify Customer with a justification and estimated retention timeline.

Backups, Snapshots, and Disaster Recovery
- Backups: Data that is deleted from primary storage may persist in backup media for the Backup Window. Provider will make reasonable efforts to purge deleted data from backups during normal backup rotation and retention processes.
- Rapid restoration: Provider maintains procedures to restore data from backups for a limited period; restoration of deleted data will follow Customer instructions and applicable policies.
- Encrypted backups: Backups are encrypted in transit and at rest. Where encryption keys are managed by Customer (BYOK), Provider will inform Customer about any key-related implications for deletion from encrypted backups.

Data Minimization and Periodic Review
- Provider will support Customer controls to minimize retention by exposing retention configuration in the Console and APIs.
- Provider will run quarterly retention reviews and surface retention anomalies (unexpectedly long-lived datasets) to Customers via the Console and optional audit reports.

Audit Rights and Evidence
- Customer may, once per 12-month period, request evidence that Provider’s retention and deletion practices conform to this annex. Evidence may include redacted logs, job IDs, summary deletion reports, and descriptions of retention operations.
- Where Customer requires a SOC/ISO report or a third-party audit, Provider will coordinate redacted extracts or provide attestations consistent with the Agreement and confidentiality constraints.

Security Controls for Deletion Workflows
- All deletion operations are logged with immutable job IDs and access controls.
- Deletion tooling requires multi-person authorization for bulk or system-level erasures in Dedicated environments.
- Role-based access controls limit who can trigger permanent deletion; triggers are subject to MFA and change-control procedures.

Notifications and Escalations
- Provider will notify Customer upon: (a) receipt of a Deletion Request; (b) completion of deletion from active storage; (c) completion of deletion from backups per Backup Window estimates; and (d) any exception, delay, or legal hold that prevents standard processing.
- For SLA misses (when Provider cannot meet the timelines above), Provider will provide a root-cause analysis and remediation plan within 10 business days of the miss.

Customer Responsibilities
- Customers must specify the scope of Deletion Requests with sufficient detail (data identifiers, date ranges, storage buckets, tenant IDs).
- For Private deployments, Customer must provide access, credentials, or a change window to enable Provider assistance when requested.
- Customers are responsible for configuring retention settings in the Console if they wish to use non-default periods; Provider is not liable for data retained due to misconfiguration by Customer.

Fees and Exceptional Work
- Standard deletion handling described herein is included in the Agreement. Provider reserves the right to charge reasonable fees for exceptionally large or manual deletion efforts (bulk restores followed by deletions, long-tail forensic purges) where the effort exceeds normal operational costs. Any such fees will be quoted in advance and require Customer approval.

Change Management and Versioning
- Provider may update this annex to reflect operational improvements, legal changes, or product features. Material changes that reduce Customer rights require Customer notice and will be subject to the change control provisions in the Agreement.

Contact and Escalation Matrix
Primary contact for deletion/SLO matters: security-ops@redwood.ai
Escalation: 
- Legal: legal@redwood.ai
- Customer Success: cs-ops@redwood.ai

Appendix: Example Deletion Workflow (Hosted API)
1. Customer files Deletion Request via Console or Support ticket with required identifiers.
2. Provider acknowledges within 24 hours and creates Deletion Job (ID: DJ-XXXXX).
3. Deletion Job executes against primary storage; confirmation logged and notification sent to Customer.
4. Job schedules purge in backup rotation; Provider records Backup Purge Estimate and notifies Customer.
5. Provider provides attestation after both primary and backup purges complete or after Backup Window elapses.
